Visualizer for Spotify

Is there a visualizer for Spotify on Mac?

By Syd Lawrence, a visual artist and developer who makes Vibresia. Facts last checked 2 November 2026; updated 2 November 2026.

Not built in, as far as we can find: Spotify's help and download pages don't mention a visualiser, and Canvas, the looping clips on some tracks, is a video an artist adds rather than something that moves with the music. To get visuals that follow Spotify on a Mac, use an app that listens to the Mac's sound. Vibresia, which we make, does that for free.

What Spotify has instead

Spotify's own visual is Canvas: a short looping clip an artist can add to each track. It's made in advance, so it loops the same way whatever the song is doing. Spotify's desktop app once ran third-party apps through a directory called App Finder, but Spotify stopped taking new ones in March 2014 and phased them out of the desktop app in early 2015.

Developers building their own visualisers have lost a route too. In November 2024 Spotify cut new apps off from its Web API's audio-analysis and audio-features data, which some visualisers used to know where the beats were. A visualiser that listens to the sound itself doesn't depend on any of that.

How to get visuals for Spotify on a Mac

Vibresia is a free Mac app that listens to the Mac's system audio, so it doesn't need Spotify to support it. Install it, allow it to hear system audio the first time it asks, and play something in Spotify. The visuals follow the music straight away: it picks out the beat, the bass, mids and treble and the tempo on the Mac, and nothing is uploaded.

It has 18 built-in scenes, and Auto Scan moves between them on the beat. If you want something of your own, a scene is a single GLSL function, or you can describe one to an AI assistant and have it written for you. It needs macOS 14.2 or later, Apple silicon.

Why system audio is the way to do it

A visualiser built into one music app only sees that app. Apple's own visualiser is a good example: it only works with songs playing in the Music app. Listening to the Mac's system audio instead means one visualiser works with Spotify, with every other music app, with a browser tab and with a film, and keeps going when you switch between them.

Questions people ask

Does Spotify have a visualizer?

Not one that Spotify documents for its Mac app. Canvas clips loop the same way whatever the music does. An app that listens to the Mac's system audio, such as Vibresia, gives you visuals that follow Spotify.

Does Vibresia work with the Spotify web player?

Yes. Vibresia hears the Mac's system audio, so it reacts to Spotify in the browser as well as in the Mac app.

Is Vibresia free?

Yes. Every feature is free, with no account and no trial, and the code is open source under the MIT licence.
